title: Research: one shared call at block 3, which two-term parts finish, which remove (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds one package, `research/complex-m3-shared-call-finish-or-remove`: an exact table, in the frame game at 3
address bits, of what one array can hold in the output of a call that it shares with a second array. Among the
two-term parts tested (two kinds; coefficients 1, −1, 2 and 1/2 for the first kind and 1, −1 and 2 for the
second), none can be both finished by a last call and removed from the other array's last call. Checked by
computer; not a theorem about all programs. No new κ; no record, target or frozen package changes.

| Finding | Game | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Two-term parts of kinds A and B of one shared middle call at 3 address bits, coefficient 1 (10,752 free elements each): 128 finishable by the last call alone and 639 removable by a call that could be a last call (kind A), 0 and 128 (kind B), none both | frame game | checked by computer in exact rational arithmetic; every case was also run one at a time with no symmetry reduction |
| The kind A rule. Same frame: finishable by the call alone exactly when 1 + c·g is invertible, removable exactly when it is not. Other frames: neither | frame game | checked by computer on all 9,983 tested cases for each of c = 1, −1, 2 and 1/2, none both; no proof by hand |
| Kind B with c = −1 and c = 2: none finishable; the same 128 parts removable with −1, none with 2 | frame game | checked by computer on all 9,984 tested cases each |
| With a free step after the last call, 128 more kind A parts are finished at c = 1 (512 at 2 and at 1/2), none of them removable | frame game | checked by computer, each identity term by term; that the list is complete is local only |
| Kind A parts on adjacent frames are removable at c = ±1 only by four calls that cannot be a last call | frame game | checked by computer |
| One first call and one shared call are enough, by symmetry | frame game | argued by hand; the counts, a second shared call and 368 cases of the map are checked by computer |
| The same rule with one spare address bit (4 address bits) | frame game | checked by computer on a seeded sample of 100 cases only |
| A 2 in 5 at three directions with one spare address bit (1.66e-1, a saving in the paid calls of one unit, not a κ) | engine game | open; no evidence either way |

Remaining obligations: no person has checked the table, the rule or the symmetry argument. The table is a result
about the cases it lists: parts with three or more terms, a first call that reads a combination of the raw
input, last calls repaired against each other, other arrangements of the five calls, and the engine game itself
are not covered. At 3 address bits a 2 in 5 was already excluded by #4628, so nothing new is excluded.

## Task and overlap

- Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8. The catalogue's context still describes
  #5599; the selected record at this base is Jerry Chen / CubeJerry's #7000 with the paired #7001, which this
  package does not touch. Card `scope-navigation` (method "Index one tightly related family of obstructions with
  explicit excluded and open hypotheses"), `scope_status: changed`: the package also adds a result that is not on
  main (the table and its rule). Reason in `TASK.json`.
- No live inputs. Provenance rows: the task catalogue and the READMEs of #4628, #4743, #4688, #4751 and #4797.
- Nearest work. The shape: eumemic's negative results (#288), Jose Manuel's bound for five-call circuits (#2108:
  at least four mixing blocks) and my earlier note (#4628: s ≥ 14W/5 at block 3, proved in Lean, which excludes
  2 in 5 there). The conflict was met on examples in October 2026. lee-phys's two-image prefix (#4688) is
  invertible with U + 2V and has a kernel with U + V. For a five-call preparation built on that prefix,
  JoyboyBrian showed that with the invertible coefficient no change of the fresh input's free feed repairs it
  (#4751), and that with coefficient 1 a free decoder leaves no contamination from the fresh owner but only a
  partial channel (#4797). Nick Petalas (#4825) and Dugongue (#4885) found that channel's rank. Reading these as
  one conflict is my reading, not a statement of those notes. They work in the engine game with every phase
  kept, and this package works in the frame game.
- The same finite geometry is already on the hub under another name. Dugongue's #4743 has a census of it at
  three directions (the group of order 10,752, the 14 neighbouring frames, the stabiliser of order 768) and uses
  this "symplectic quotient" as a search coordinate system; zxv's #5283 defines frames the same way.
- On other questions: Nick Petalas's open #7551 (a cut ceiling on the same graph), Dugongue's atlas (#5803) and
  the five-array shared port of Chris R (#4856) and JoyboyBrian (#5491). The one unit claimed at three directions
  (#4813, 5 in 14) was withdrawn by its author on 23 October 2026; its folder on main still shows the original
  text.
- This package adds the table and the kind A rule with a coefficient, and links the earlier work instead of
  repeating it.
- Overlap search, 16 November 2026: the titles and bodies of all 7,102 pull requests and the 5,653 folder names
  under `research/` at the base. I found no table of this kind. The hub's nearest word to a spare address bit is
  "spectator"; 330 pull requests use it and I did not read their bodies, so I do not claim that no small unit was
  studied with one. This is bounded coverage, not a novelty certificate; Discussions were not searched.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-m3-shared-call-finish-or-remove --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-m3-shared-call-finish-or-remove
# = python3 -B research/complex-m3-shared-call-finish-or-remove/verify.py --part controls       (PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_CONTROLS)
#   ... --part main            (PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_MAIN)
#   ... --part poststep        (PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_POSTSTEP)
#   ... --part symmetry        (PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_SYMMETRY)
#   ... --part coefficients    (PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_COEFFICIENTS)
#   ... --part spare           (PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_SPARE)
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/complex-m3-shared-call-finish-or-remove --check-source-history
```

Standard library only, exact rational arithmetic, no file read or written. With Python 3.12.13 on an Apple M4
(macOS) the six registered parts take about 3, 38, 4, 42, 85 and 22 seconds and under 30 MB each. In a clone of
the hub's main at `e54523517d`, `scripts/research_package.py` passes the metadata check
(`PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`) and runs the six registered commands with Python 3.12.13
(`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`), and `scripts/check_research_commit.py` passes on the commit that adds the
package, with `--check-source-history` (`PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`).

Controls:
- the solver finds the plain third call and refuses a target two calls away;
- arithmetic modulo 2^61 − 1 gives the same answers on 92 seeded cases;
- three wrong variants of the rule are each rejected;
- the symmetry map is tested case by case with a symmetry that does not commute with the first call;
- the program refuses to run under `-O`, where its assert statements would be skipped.

Local only: two AI reviewers rebuilt the counts of an earlier form of the table from the README's definitions
with their own programs, which are not in this package. Between them they found the two corrections that are
now in section 5 (a free step after the last call; removing calls that cannot be a last call).

Not registered: `--part full`, every case one at a time with no symmetry reduction; I ran it once in four
quarters of about a minute each, with the same totals. Not run: the 20,643,840 cases at 4 address bits (a sample
of 100 only); any other coefficient; a free step after the last call for kind B; the hub's `find_overlap.py`
helper (I used my own search, described above); Lean.

Hosted CI: at this base the `plan` job fails on one of the hub's own tests, so the package replay is skipped for
new pull requests. I did not retrigger it. The local replay above is the evidence.

A remark on method, not evidence (local only: the runs and the files are not public and not in this package).
The table came out of nine runs in which AI agents carried ideas for sharing work into this game, eight of them
from other fields. None gave a program that beats the plain way at three directions, and six arrived separately
at this arrangement. Before looking at which cases were removable, the AI agent I work with wrote a guess for
the rule in a dated file, with a confidence of 75 %, and the comparison matched. Review by other AI agents then
asked two things the guess had not asked, and both changed the table. The README has the paragraph.

## Credit

On the hub: eumemic (#288); Jose Manuel (#2108); lee-phys (#4688); Yiyang, whose phase repair (#4710) the October
thread built on; Dugongue (#4743, #4885, #5803); JoyboyBrian (#4751, #4797, #5491); Nick Petalas (#4825, #7551);
Chris R (#4856); alephnan (#6714); zxv (#5283). OpenAI for the cost model, the call and its 2-point kernel.

Fields the local runs drew on, none of which gave a saving: coded caching (Maddah-Ali and Niesen) and
interference alignment (in Cadambe and Jafar's form); catalytic computing (Buhrman, Cleve, Koucký, Loff and
Speelman; Cook and Mertz) with Bennett's uncomputation; Strassen's and Pan's fast matrix multiplication; the
transform splittings of Winograd, Rader and Bluestein; branch and sector bookkeeping from quantum circuits;
storage codes (Dimakis and co-authors) and secret sharing (Shamir); Maschke's averaging over a group; addition
chains (Yao; Pippenger) with Borodin and Moenck's remainder trees.

Substantial AI assistance: I did this work with the help of AI agents (Anthropic's Claude). The programs, the
searches, the arguments and the text were written by the agents under my direction. No independent human review
of this package is claimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

In README (`## Open next questions`) and `TASK.json`. The smallest useful follow-up: the same arrangement at 4
address bits with every coefficient left free and the two last outputs read together. It matters because a
2 in 5 with one spare address bit is the smallest shape at three directions that no bound I know excludes (a
saving of 1.66e-1 in the paid calls of one unit, not a κ). Blocked by nothing but size: 20,643,840 free elements
before symmetry. Two smaller ones: a proof that a kind A part on two different frames is never finishable by the
call alone; a proof that a call which exchanges the frames of the two terms removes a kind B part when c = ±1.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

At this base the `plan` job fails for new pull requests on the hub's own test
`test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record` (as far as I can tell from the job logs of #7551 and #7627:
`docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 while the selected record is #7000), so no package replay runs.

  5 in 14: #4813.
- My repository: https://github.com/jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean at commit `0788bc6568` (3 November
  2026): `research/frame-packing-two-arrays/` (the frame game, the completion of frame-game programs, the
  negative control), `research/moonshot-block4-block5/` (the 2 in 7 dilemma) and
  `research/block-bounds-and-new-rules/` (spare rows, the 2.4883 lower bound, the open case).
